# Procurement Review Workflow

Procurement Review Workflow refers to a structured sequence of steps designed to analyze contracts, ensure compliance, and manage vendor relationships efficiently in procurement settings. It typically begins with automated clause extraction, identifying key contract elements such as payment terms, liability, and delivery schedules. Next, redlining tools highlight deviations from standard templates, enabling legal teams to review and negotiate changes quickly. Finally, contracts proceed through staged approvals before vendor onboarding.

This workflow balances speed and accuracy: automation accelerates reviews but requires careful rule tuning to avoid missing critical deviations. A typical example: out of 200 contracts monthly, automated extraction flags 30 with atypical clauses; after redlining, 10 require human negotiation, reducing overall review time by 40%.

Common failure modes include false negatives in clause detection, conflicting edits in redlining, and delays due to unclear approval hierarchies. Continuous monitoring and iterative model updates help mitigate these risks, ensuring procurement compliance and vendor satisfaction.
